According to the J7 Large Communities’ Task Force Against Antisemitism, 2025 was the deadliest year for antisemitic attacks around the world since 1994.
Beth Bailey writes on the United Nations, worldwide antisemitism, and regions in conflict for Fox News.

title: Republican Byron Donalds and Democrat David Jolly set to square off for Florida’s governorship
summary: Donalds and Jolly easily won their primaries, NBC News projects, as Donalds enters the general election with a big financial advantage.
story: ORLANDO, Fla. — Florida’s primary voters went with the favorites in both parties Tuesday night, setting up a long-expected clash to determine who will be the state’s next governor after eight years of Ron DeSantis.
See live results here

On the Republican side, Rep. Byron Donalds, who has been endorsed by President Donald Trump, outran a crowded GOP field to win his party’s nomination, NBC News projects, while Republican-turned-Democrat David Jolly, a former member of Congress, won his primary.

Both outcomes, which were expected, officially kick off a general election showdown in which Republicans are trying to extend their decadeslong grip on Florida’s governorship, while Jolly and Democrats are out to prove the longtime battleground state has not gotten totally out of reach for their party.
Republicans control all levels of state government in Florida and have not lost a race for governor since 1994.

Even as Republicans have dominated the state’s gubernatorial contests, Democrats largely remained competitive — until DeSantis, who could not run again because of term limits, won his 2022 re-election bid by more than 20 percentage points. The historic margin prompted a huge Republican victory lap and claims that Florida had changed since its days as the country’s largest swing state.
Jolly’s candidacy is seen as a test case for whether that is the state’s new, GOP-dominated political identity or whether Democrats can rebuild after the eight-year DeSantis era.

Jolly, a former Republican member of Congress, later changed parties and is seen as a more moderate Democrat. That’s something many in the party believed was needed after more progressive nominees, including the Democratic nominee who narrowly lost to DeSantis in 2018, came up short in high-profile governor’s races.

Jolly faced only nominal competition for the Democratic nomination after Orange County Mayor Jerry Demings suspended his campaign in June following a cancer diagnosis. Democratic former state Rep. Dottie Joseph was also in the race but never really gained momentum.
Meanwhile, the Republican primary contest was heated and personal.
Donalds raised a staggering nearly $100 million and held a huge lead in most public polling after Trump endorsed him in May, but three other GOP candidates ran campaigns relentlessly attacking him.

James Fishback, a controversial right-wing figure new to politics, spent the campaign criticizing Donalds, at times using shocking language designed to generate attention. The Republican Party of Florida criticized Fishback in June for leveling what it called “antisemitic and racist attacks.”

Fishback also faced criticism over his past business dealings and his time running a youth debate program. NBC News reported last year that Fishback’s early political rise was tied to former DeSantis advisers and that at least one school district cut ties with the debate program he ran following sexual misconduct allegations. Fishback has denied wrongdoing.

Fishback held dozens of rallies across the state and gained support from younger male voters in particular, according to pre-election polling. His endorsements included, among others, that of the white nationalist personality Nick Fuentes.

The two other most visible GOP candidates were Lt. Gov. Jay Collins and former state House Speaker Paul Renner, whose campaigns spent most of their time attacking each other as they tried, and failed, to gain traction against Donalds.

Collins was appointed by DeSantis last year to be his lieutenant governor, and he was seen as the person at that time whom DeSantis wanted to succeed him as governor. The relationship, however, quickly fell apart, and DeSantis ultimately did not support his campaign.
DeSantis did not endorse in the race to replace him.

Renner was speaker of the state House for two years during DeSantis’ governorship and helped him secure several policy wins that later went on to be the basis for DeSantis’ 2024 presidential campaign.
In the final weeks of the race, DeSantis said he thought Renner would be a “really good” governor, but he stopped short of a full endorsement.

title: Democratic socialist Angie Nixon upsets Alex Vindman in Florida’s Democratic Senate primary
summary: NBC News projects that Nixon, a state lawmaker, will face GOP Sen. Ashley Moody, who was appointed to replace Secretary of State Marco Rubio, in the general election.
story: Progressive state Rep. Angie Nixon scored a major upset over former National Security Council aide Alex Vindman in the Florida Democratic Senate primary, NBC News projects, setting up a general election race against Republican Sen. Ashley Moody.

Vindman, a retired lieutenant colonel and Iraq War veteran who rose to prominence as a witness during President Donald Trump’s 2019 impeachment hearings, was viewed as a heavy favorite against Nixon, a member of the Democratic Socialists of America, heading into Tuesday’s contest.
Vindman raised $16 million for his campaign, a significant number for a Democrat in red-leaning Florida, while Nixon brought in just over $900,000.
“We did it ya’ll,” Nixon posted Tuesday night on X. “Thank you to every person that put their heart into this campaign.”

Vindman was recruited to run for the seat by the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee in an effort to expand its map during a midterm election cycle that is expected to be favorable for the party.
In a statement, Vindman said Nixon “ran a strong campaign.”
“I will be standing by her side in the fight against Ashley Moody,” he continued. “I hope you’ll join me.”
The DSCC also released a statement supportive of Nixon after her victory.

“Angie Nixon has dedicated her career to fighting for Florida. A lifelong native of Jacksonville and a former union organizer, Angie’s dedication to put working families first runs deep — and now, she’s running to take that fight to the Senate,” Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., and DSCC Chair Kristen Gillibrand, D-N.Y., said in a joint statement. “Ashley Moody’s votes have cost Florida, from her siding with private insurance companies over Floridians to ripping away health care. In November, Florida will have a clear choice at the ballot.”
Meanwhile, the National Republican Senatorial Campaign Committee quickly took a swipe at Nixon.
“Florida will never elect a socialist to the US Senate and we look forward to Ashley Moody’s victory in November,” spokesman Nick Puglia said.
Nixon regularly criticized Vindman for only recently having moved to Florida and said her campaign was an attempt to prove that insurgent progressive politics has a place in Florida politics.
“Florida: the choice is OURS,” Nixon posted on social media as part of her closing message. “We will decide our future, not billionaire donors or the establishment politics of DC.”

Nixon is an advocate for cutting U.S. aid to Israel, a controversial position in a state with the country’s third-largest Jewish population. Her stance put her at odds with members of her own party at times and was in contrast to Vindman, a Jewish immigrant born in Soviet Ukraine.

Nixon introduced a resolution in the state House calling for a “de-escalation and ceasefire in the state of Israel and occupied Palestine.” She also said she would have supported a congressional resolution in July that would have stripped $3.3 billion in military aid to Israel.

“I would have voted in support of that, because we cannot continue to send money to countries that are violating international law, that are violating human rights, that are actively destroying,” she said Friday on WMNF radio of Tampa. “Throughout my adult career, I have fought for the safety and the well-being and the humanity of all people. And me stating this does not make me antisemitic at all.”

Vindman drew national attention when, as an aide to the National Security Council, he gave congressional testimony about a 2019 call between Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as Trump was pushing for an investigation into Joe Biden, who at the time was a Democratic candidate for president.
The testimony helped launch Trump’s first impeachment by the House. Trump was ultimately acquitted by the Senate, and Vindman was later fired from the NSC.
Vindman had largely ignored Nixon during the primary — the two never met for a debate — and tried to focus on Moody.

Moody and Nixon are vying to serve the final two years of the term Secretary of State Marco Rubio won in 2022. Gov. Ron DeSantis appointed Moody to the seat last year after Trump selected Rubio for his Cabinet.
She easily fended off several challengers to win her Republican primary Tuesday, NBC News projects.

title: GOP Rep. Cory Mills loses his Florida primary amid investigations
summary: Mills lost to Republican Ryan Elijah, NBC News projects, while facing House Ethics Committee and Justice Department investigations. Mills has denied wrongdoing.
story: Republican Rep. Cory Mills has lost his primary in Florida, NBC News projects, amid a swirl of investigations and negative publicity and despite running with the backing of President Donald Trump.

Former television journalist Ryan Elijah captured the Republican nomination over Mills in Florida’s 7th District, a seat Trump carried by 12 percentage points in 2024. Democrats have hoped to make it competitive this fall, especially if Mills were on the ballot.
With more than 80% of the expected vote counted, Elijah had 46% of the GOP primary vote to 34% for Mills.

Unlike other incumbents who have fallen short this year for being on the wrong side of intraparty divides, Mills was defeated as he has been dogged by multiple investigations, including a House Ethics Committee probe into allegations of sexual misconduct and campaign finance violations, as well as a Justice Department investigation into his finances. He has denied wrongdoing.

Despite his struggles, Mills still got Trump’s endorsement. The loss makes him the latest member of a relatively rare set of Republican candidates who lost GOP primaries even with Trump’s blessing. Republican Rep. Andy Ogles of Tennessee also lost his primary this month with Trump’s support.
Mills is the 11th House member — seven Democrats and four Republicans — to lose a primary this year, an unusually high number.

Elijah ran with support from a slew of prominent Florida Republicans who have either directly or indirectly referred to Mills’ woes. Republican Reps. Anna Paulina Luna and Mike Haridopolos took the rare step of endorsing against a House colleague, putting out a statement that emphasized Elijah’s character.
“We need leaders in Congress who serve with integrity, energy, and an unwavering commitment to the people who sent them there,” they wrote.

Facing a clear threat to his political career, Mills struggled to raise money, pulling in less than $900,000 through late July. That was still twice what Elijah raised during the same period, though less than the takes of the vast majority of House members seeking re-election, according to an NBC News analysis of campaign finance reports.

Mills, an Army veteran, was a military contractor before he made a successful bid for Congress in 2022. His House tenure has included both the Ethics Committee and Justice Department investigations and bipartisan calls for him to resign this spring and previous allegations from an ex-girlfriend that he harassed her. Mills has repeatedly denied he has done anything wrong in all of those cases.
While neither candidate spent much on the airwaves, Elijah significantly outspent Mills on ads: $82,000 to $12,000, according to the ad-tracking firm AdImpact.
Bale Dalton, a former NASA official, is projected to win the Democratic primary. He defeated former Rep. Alan Grayson, who was seeking another return to Congress.

title: Hayden Panettiere’s ex-partner Wladimir Klitschko shares ‘profound shock’ in tribute
summary: “She left this world far too soon,” wrote Klitschko, the Ukrainian boxer and father of their child, Kaya.
story: Actor Hayden Panettiere’s former partner said Tuesday their family is “going through a time of profound shock and grief” following her death.
Wladimir Klitschko, the Ukrainian boxer and brother of the mayor of Kyiv, paid tribute to his ex-fiancée on Instagram.

“The announcement of Hayden’s tragic death saddens me deeply. She left this world far too soon,” he wrote. “Hayden was, although no longer my partner, an important part of my life and the mother of our daughter, Kaya.”

Klitschko shared an image of their daughter happily sitting on her mother’s shoulders as he paid tribute to Panettiere’s “incredible career through immense talent, while also facing the darker sides of a very demanding industry.”

“Nothing will erase the times we shared or the place she had in our lives. To our daughter Kaya, I will always speak of her mother with respect and make sure she remembers the person she was,” Klitschko wrote.

“I extend my deepest condolences to Hayden’s parents, her friends, and her fans, who are also grieving today. Young and talented people like Hayden should not leave this world so soon,” he added. “Rest easy, Hayden. May you find eternal peace.”

title: Two Trump-backed candidates lose, Debbie Wasserman Schultz wins in Tuesday’s House primaries
summary: Democratic Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz has won her party’s nomination for re-election, NBC News projects, while two Republican House candidates backed by President Donald Trump lost their primary bids in Florida on Tuesday.
story: Democratic Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz has won her party’s nomination for re-election, NBC News projects, while two Republican House candidates backed by President Donald Trump lost their primary bids in Florida on Tuesday.

Republican Gov. Ron DeSantis and other party leaders redrew Wasserman Schultz’s current district and three other Democratic seats into four new GOP-leaning districts the party is hoping to flip in November.

The move prompted Wasserman Schultz, a former chair of the Democratic National Committee, to run in the state’s 20th District, which has long been represented by Black Democrats and is vacant because former Rep. Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick resigned after being indicted and accused of stealing millions in Covid relief. She has denied wrongdoing.

Wasserman Schultz’s decision sparked some frustration among Black Democrats. Cherfilus-McCormick ran again for the seat, and the other candidates were all Black Democrats: activist Elijah Manley, who was backed by Rep. Ro Khanna; former Broward County Mayor Dale Holness; and Luther “Uncle Luke” Campbell, the hip hop star and former 2 Live Crew band member.

But ultimately, Wasserman Schultz bested the crowded field and avoided adding her name to the list of incumbents who’ve lost their re-elections this year. Her Democratic colleague, Rep. Jared Moskowitz, also won his primary in the battleground 25th District, brushing aside a challenge from the left by Oliver Larkin, a former union organizer and democratic socialist.
But Republican Rep. Cory Mills fell short.

Former television journalist Ryan Elijah defeated the incumbent in the state’s 7th District, as Mills came into the race wounded by a slew of controversies, including a House Ethics Committee probe into sexual misconduct and campaign finance violations and a Justice Department investigation, NBC News previously reported. Mills has denied wrongdoing.
Mills lost despite getting Trump’s support earlier in his campaign. Meanwhile, Republican Catalina Lauf was the other Trump-backed candidate to lose a primary bid Tuesday.

She received Trump’s blessing late last week but fell short to Jim Schwartzel, a businessman and local conservative talk radio station owner, in the Naples-area 19th District. The crowded primary included two former members of Congress who previously left Washington amid ethics concerns and subsequently moved to the Florida district to restart their career: Former North Carolina Rep. Madison Cawthorn and former New York Rep. Chris Collins.

The field also included former Illinois state Sen. Jim Oberweis, against whom Lauf ran in a 2020 Illinois congressional primary before both decamped for Florida. Schwartzel is now the favorite in the race to replace Republican Rep. Byron Donalds, who is running for governor.

The 16th District, which includes St. Petersburg and Bradenton, featured far less drama, with Sydney Gruters, a former nonprofit executive and the wife of Republican National Committee Chairman Joe Gruters, clinching the Republican nod in that red district. She’s the heavy favorite to replace the retiring Rep. Vern Buchanan.
Austin Rogers, who worked for Sen. Rick Scott, won the Republican nod in the open, heavily Republican 2nd District.

On the Democratic side, Oliver Gilbert, the former Miami Gardens mayor and Miami-Dade County Commissioner, narrowly bested state Sen. Shevrin Jones in the North Miami, Democratic-leaning district where Rep. Frederica Wilson is retiring.

While the most immediate implications from Tuesday’s elections are these primaries in largely safe seats, where the winners are the heavy favorites to join Congress next year, a handful of important matchups were set in potential battleground races.
In Florida, Moskowitz is set to face former Boca Raton Mayor Scott Singer in one of four Democratic-held districts that Republicans are seriously contesting in November.
In the Orlando-area 9th District, Democratic Rep. Darren Soto’s Republican opponent has yet to be decided, with the top two candidates separated by less than a thousand votes.
Democratic Rep. Kathy Castor will face off against former Republican state Rep. Mike Beltran in a redrawn Tampa Bay-area 14th District.

And Democrat Pia Dandiya, a former educator, will run against Republican Marine veteran Casey Askar in the Palm Beach County-area 22nd District. All four of these seats were redrawn as ones that Trump would have won by at least 9 points in the 2024 election.

There are also a small handful of Republican-held seats Democrats are looking to contest. In the South Florida 27th District, Democrat and former Miami TV personality Elliot Rodriguez will try to defeat Republican Rep. María Elvira Salazar.
And Republican Rep. Anna Paulina Luna will face off against Democratic nomination is retired Army veteran Leela Gray in the Tampa Bay-area 13th District.

That was still twice what Elijah raised during the same period, though less than the takes of the vast majority of House members seeking re-election, according to an NBC News analysis of campaign finance reports.

Mills, an Army veteran, was a military contractor before he made a successful bid for Congress in 2022. His House tenure has included both the Ethics Committee and Justice Department investigations and bipartisan calls for him to resign this spring and previous allegations from an ex-girlfriend that he harassed her. Mills has repeatedly denied he has done anything wrong in all of those cases.
While neither candidate spent much on the airwaves, Elijah significantly outspent Mills on ads: $82,000 to $12,000, according to the ad-tracking firm AdImpact.
Bale Dalton, a former NASA official, is projected to win the Democratic primary. He defeated former Rep. Alan Grayson, who was seeking another return to Congress.

title: Democratic socialist Angie Nixon upsets Alex Vindman in Florida’s Democratic Senate primary
summary: NBC News projects that Nixon, a state lawmaker, will face GOP Sen. Ashley Moody, who was appointed to replace Secretary of State Marco Rubio, in the general election.
story: Progressive state Rep. Angie Nixon scored a major upset over former National Security Council aide Alex Vindman in the Florida Democratic Senate primary, NBC News projects, setting up a general election race against Republican Sen. Ashley Moody.

Vindman, a retired lieutenant colonel and Iraq War veteran who rose to prominence as a witness during President Donald Trump’s 2019 impeachment hearings, was viewed as a heavy favorite against Nixon, a member of the Democratic Socialists of America, heading into Tuesday’s contest.
Vindman raised $16 million for his campaign, a significant number for a Democrat in red-leaning Florida, while Nixon brought in just over $900,000.
“We did it ya’ll,” Nixon posted Tuesday night on X. “Thank you to every person that put their heart into this campaign.”

Vindman was recruited to run for the seat by the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee in an effort to expand its map during a midterm election cycle that is expected to be favorable for the party.
In a statement, Vindman said Nixon “ran a strong campaign.”
“I will be standing by her side in the fight against Ashley Moody,” he continued. “I hope you’ll join me.”
The DSCC also released a statement supportive of Nixon after her victory.

“Angie Nixon has dedicated her career to fighting for Florida. A lifelong native of Jacksonville and a former union organizer, Angie’s dedication to put working families first runs deep — and now, she’s running to take that fight to the Senate,” Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., and DSCC Chair Kristen Gillibrand, D-N.Y., said in a joint statement. “Ashley Moody’s votes have cost Florida, from her siding with private insurance companies over Floridians to ripping away health care. In November, Florida will have a clear choice at the ballot.”
Meanwhile, the National Republican Senatorial Campaign Committee quickly took a swipe at Nixon.
“Florida will never elect a socialist to the US Senate and we look forward to Ashley Moody’s victory in November,” spokesman Nick Puglia said.
Nixon regularly criticized Vindman for only recently having moved to Florida and said her campaign was an attempt to prove that insurgent progressive politics has a place in Florida politics.
“Florida: the choice is OURS,” Nixon posted on social media as part of her closing message. “We will decide our future, not billionaire donors or the establishment politics of DC.”

Nixon is an advocate for cutting U.S. aid to Israel, a controversial position in a state with the country’s third-largest Jewish population. Her stance put her at odds with members of her own party at times and was in contrast to Vindman, a Jewish immigrant born in Soviet Ukraine.

Nixon introduced a resolution in the state House calling for a “de-escalation and ceasefire in the state of Israel and occupied Palestine.” She also said she would have supported a congressional resolution in July that would have stripped $3.3 billion in military aid to Israel.

“I would have voted in support of that, because we cannot continue to send money to countries that are violating international law, that are violating human rights, that are actively destroying,” she said Friday on WMNF radio of Tampa. “Throughout my adult career, I have fought for the safety and the well-being and the humanity of all people. And me stating this does not make me antisemitic at all.”

Vindman drew national attention when, as an aide to the National Security Council, he gave congressional testimony about a 2019 call between Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as Trump was pushing for an investigation into Joe Biden, who at the time was a Democratic candidate for president.
The testimony helped launch Trump’s first impeachment by the House. Trump was ultimately acquitted by the Senate, and Vindman was later fired from the NSC.
Vindman had largely ignored Nixon during the primary — the two never met for a debate — and tried to focus on Moody.

Moody and Nixon are vying to serve the final two years of the term Secretary of State Marco Rubio won in 2022. Gov. Ron DeSantis appointed Moody to the seat last year after Trump selected Rubio for his Cabinet.
She easily fended off several challengers to win her Republican primary Tuesday, NBC News projects.

title: Republican Byron Donalds and Democrat David Jolly set to square off for Florida’s governorship
summary: Donalds and Jolly easily won their primaries, NBC News projects, as Donalds enters the general election with a big financial advantage.
story: ORLANDO, Fla. — Florida’s primary voters went with the favorites in both parties Tuesday night, setting up a long-expected clash to determine who will be the state’s next governor after eight years of Ron DeSantis.
See live results here

On the Republican side, Rep. Byron Donalds, who has been endorsed by President Donald Trump, outran a crowded GOP field to win his party’s nomination, NBC News projects, while Republican-turned-Democrat David Jolly, a former member of Congress, won his primary.

Both outcomes, which were expected, officially kick off a general election showdown in which Republicans are trying to extend their decadeslong grip on Florida’s governorship, while Jolly and Democrats are out to prove the longtime battleground state has not gotten totally out of reach for their party.
Republicans control all levels of state government in Florida and have not lost a race for governor since 1994.

Even as Republicans have dominated the state’s gubernatorial contests, Democrats largely remained competitive — until DeSantis, who could not run again because of term limits, won his 2022 re-election bid by more than 20 percentage points. The historic margin prompted a huge Republican victory lap and claims that Florida had changed since its days as the country’s largest swing state.
Jolly’s candidacy is seen as a test case for whether that is the state’s new, GOP-dominated political identity or whether Democrats can rebuild after the eight-year DeSantis era.

Jolly, a former Republican member of Congress, later changed parties and is seen as a more moderate Democrat. That’s something many in the party believed was needed after more progressive nominees, including the Democratic nominee who narrowly lost to DeSantis in 2018, came up short in high-profile governor’s races.

Jolly faced only nominal competition for the Democratic nomination after Orange County Mayor Jerry Demings suspended his campaign in June following a cancer diagnosis. Democratic former state Rep. Dottie Joseph was also in the race but never really gained momentum.
Meanwhile, the Republican primary contest was heated and personal.
Donalds raised a staggering nearly $100 million and held a huge lead in most public polling after Trump endorsed him in May, but three other GOP candidates ran campaigns relentlessly attacking him.

James Fishback, a controversial right-wing figure new to politics, spent the campaign criticizing Donalds, at times using shocking language designed to generate attention. The Republican Party of Florida criticized Fishback in June for leveling what it called “antisemitic and racist attacks.”

Fishback also faced criticism over his past business dealings and his time running a youth debate program. NBC News reported last year that Fishback’s early political rise was tied to former DeSantis advisers and that at least one school district cut ties with the debate program he ran following sexual misconduct allegations. Fishback has denied wrongdoing.

Fishback held dozens of rallies across the state and gained support from younger male voters in particular, according to pre-election polling. His endorsements included, among others, that of the white nationalist personality Nick Fuentes.

The two other most visible GOP candidates were Lt. Gov. Jay Collins and former state House Speaker Paul Renner, whose campaigns spent most of their time attacking each other as they tried, and failed, to gain traction against Donalds.

Collins was appointed by DeSantis last year to be his lieutenant governor, and he was seen as the person at that time whom DeSantis wanted to succeed him as governor. The relationship, however, quickly fell apart, and DeSantis ultimately did not support his campaign.
DeSantis did not endorse in the race to replace him.

Renner was speaker of the state House for two years during DeSantis’ governorship and helped him secure several policy wins that later went on to be the basis for DeSantis’ 2024 presidential campaign.
In the final weeks of the race, DeSantis said he thought Renner would be a “really good” governor, but he stopped short of a full endorsement.

title: DeSantis ally and appointee is arrested on child sex abuse charges
summary: Michael Caruso was removed as Palm Beach County’s clerk of courts and comptroller after his arrest was announced
story: A former Florida lawmaker and political ally of Gov. Ron DeSantis was arrested Tuesday and accused of molesting a young boy at the child’s home, on fishing excursions and while on a family cruise, arrest records show.

Michael Caruso, a 67-year-old Republican whom DeSantis appointed as Palm Beach County’s clerk of courts and comptroller a year ago, was taken into custody by local police and officers from the Florida Department of Law Enforcement.
“Being in a position of public trust provides no shield from accountability,” Attorney General James Uthmeier said in a statement Tuesday.

After the arrest was announced, DeSantis suspended Caruso from his post and noted in an executive order that the allegations include lewd or lascivious molestation, lewd or lascivious exhibition, kidnapping, child abuse causing mental injury, and luring or enticing a child.
Caruso had regular and unsupervised access to the child, a probable cause affidavit released by the governor’s office said.
Caruso is accused of preying on the boy more than half a dozen times since Thanksgiving 2024, sometimes under the guise of playing “tickle monster,” according to the affidavit.
Asked at a news conference whether he was aware of the allegations before Caruso was nominated for the Palm Beach post, DeSantis said, “Of course not.”
“He had a clean vet, he was well-regarded in the community,” the governor said.
DeSantis said that once he became aware of the allegations against Caruso, “it was a very easy decision for me to yank him from this position.”
Noting that Florida now has a death penalty for convicted pedophiles, DeSantis warned that if Caruso is found guilty of the allegations, “he is going to be in a world of hurt.”

Caruso is running for re-election in November to retain the top county post that DeSantis appointed him to. Previously, he served in the Florida House of Representatives from 2018 to 2025. And when DeSantis ran for president in 2024, Caruso campaigned with him in Iowa.
Calls to Caruso’s number, as well as his wife Tracy’s number, went unanswered Tuesday.
It was not immediately clear whether Caruso has a lawyer.
The lawyer for the alleged victim blasted DeSantis for releasing information that could potentially identify the boy.

“Child sexual abuse victims should never have identifying details about them released, and it is abhorrent that the child victim in connection with the arrest of Michael Caruso has been subjected to this breach,” Lisa Haba of The Haba Law Firm said in a statement on her firm’s website.
The chain of events that led to Caruso’s arrest began in December, when he was confronted by the boy’s father about the alleged abuse, the affidavit states.

Caruso denied abusing the child but “acknowledged that he had showered with all his own children,” the affidavit states. He stated that he’d previously been accused “of sexually inappropriate behavior, including sexual battery” by a female relative, according to the court document.
“You tell anyone, I’m going to jail,” Caruso told the child’s father, according to the affidavit.
The boy’s father also spoke with Tracy Caruso, who said her husband faced a “life in jail kinda thing” if police knew about the alleged behavior, according to the affidavit.
In February, the boy’s father confronted Caruso again about the abuse allegations while wearing a wire for the Florida Department of Law Enforcement, the affidavit states.

During that conversation, Caruso “asserted that the allegations were impossible because, in substance, sexual deviation is directed toward only one sex rather than two, and because he is attracted to women he could not be a sex offender,” the affidavit states.
Caruso urged the boy’s father to keep quiet, allegedly saying, “If you report this to the authorities, there won’t be any of me left, I can tell you that,” according to the affidavit.

title: NASA spots new crater on the moon created when a SpaceX rocket crashed
summary: A defunct part of a Falcon 9 rocket crashed into the moon uncontrolled this month at an estimated 5,400 mph. Now NASA has photos.
story: A NASA spacecraft in orbit around the moon captured dramatic images of the impact crater left when a SpaceX rocket smashed into the lunar surface this month.
The defunct upper stage of a Falcon 9 rocket crashed uncontrolled into the moon on Aug. 5 at an estimated 5,400 mph.
The roughly 10,800-pound booster had launched two landers to the moon in January 2025, then remained adrift in orbit until the impact.

NASA on Tuesday released new images of the crash site taken by its Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter on Aug. 11 and 12. Before-and-after views reveal a bright divot in the moon’s already-pockmarked terrain.

Although there were no live views of the Aug. 5 impact, researchers were able to track the rocket’s trajectory and pinpoint the expected site of the new crater along the western edge of the moon’s sunlit side.

NASA’s Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter cannot easily pick a precise spot to photograph because it circles the moon from pole to pole every two hours, while the moon rotates on its axis. That means the spacecraft must wait for its orbit to line up with a specific location as it rotates into view.
NASA said it took six days for the orbiter to fly over the SpaceX crash site.
Engineers had to tilt the spacecraft so its cameras would point toward the crater as it flew 60 miles above the lunar surface at 1 mile per second.
The new photos reveal that the crater measures about 60 feet across. Based on the length of its shadow, scientists found that it is most likely less than 10 feet deep, according to NASA.

The images also show bright and dark streaks emanating from the crater. The darker rays are surface dust and rocks that were kicked up by the collision from a depth of around 1.5 feet, according to NASA. The brighter streaks near the crater rim were formed by fresher material excavated from deeper underground after the booster smacked into the moon’s surface.
NASA said the crater center is at an elevation of roughly 1,700 feet.

Shortly after the crash, a telescope in Chile spotted a debris plume from the cosmic collision. Later, the Korea Pathfinder Lunar Orbiter, which launched in 2022 as South Korea’s first moon mission, flew over the impact site and snapped photos of the crater and the ejected material in its vicinity.

The Falcon 9 crash was only the second known case in which a rocket h unintentionally hitting the lunar surface. The moon has withstood countless impacts from asteroids and other cosmic objects over its life, but it is very rare for a human-made object to slam uncontrolled into its surface.

In 2022, what was thought to be the upper stage of a Chinese rocket that sent a test capsule to the moon in 2014 smacked into the far side of the moon, carving out a snowman-shaped double crater that the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter spotted months later. China has denied that its spacecraft was involved.
The SpaceX crash ignited fresh debates about sustainability issues in space, particularly as countries like the U.S. and China race to put their astronauts and infrastructure on the moon.
In a statement on Aug. 5, SpaceX said it tries to properly account for its hardware after missions.

“We actively work to be as responsible as possible with hardware left in space to ensure space safety, including for more complex missions,” it said. “In this case, over time, solar activity and gravity led the second stage toward the Moon. Impacts like this are rare, but they can happen with objects in these types of orbits, and we worked with NASA on the optimal disposal solution.”

title: Gov. Josh Shapiro takes a hard line against ‘predatory’ data center developers in Pennsylvania
summary: Shapiro, a potential Democratic 2028 contender, earlier welcomed data center developments. His new executive order takes a starkly different tone toward the industry.
story: Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro announced significant restrictions on data center projects Tuesday, signing an executive order to stop “predatory” backers and “bad proposals from infecting our commonwealth.”

The order, along with the warnings in his remarks for potential data center developers, marked a notable shift for Shapiro, a potential 2028 Democratic presidential contender, who had sought to encourage the industry’s build-out in his state.

“I’ve heard loud and clear from the good people of Pennsylvania as I’ve traveled our commonwealth, and I’m here to say today that we will not be bullied by these developers,” Shapiro said. “We will not be bulldozed by the lawyers working for these big tech companies. That will not happen in the commonwealth. We have a long history in Pennsylvania of industry running roughshod over our communities to make a buck — that stops with me.”

The new order mandates that data center projects must first be approved by local officials. Developers must also sign a legally binding order in which they commit to guidelines Shapiro laid out in February — which were first reported by NBC News — among them that they pay for their own power, hire locally, be transparent with local governments and adhere to high water-conservation standards.

Shapiro also said that he is removing all data center projects from his state’s fast-track permitting program and that going forward, they would be ineligible for those measures. He also said nondisclosure agreements for data center projects will not be allowed in the state under his new order.

Shapiro said in his remarks that since it announced two major data center projects in the state last year — Amazon-backed developments he touted — the state has “seen an unacceptable number of speculative proposals for data centers swamp our commonwealth — many of them led by developers who have no regard for local communities.”

Shapiro, who also faces re-election this fall, has evolved his views on data centers within the last year as the projects have faced increasing opposition in the state and nationally. Last week, The Philadelphia Inquirer wrote about how Shapiro’s early embrace of the projects was testing his high approval ratings with voters who are skeptical of the developments.
This is what it sounds like to live near a data center

Even in announcing guidelines this year to manage the data center boom, Shapiro framed the need for Pennsylvania “to play a leading role” in the battle for AI supremacy against China. He said that “no sector of our country’s economy is growing faster than data centers and artificial intelligence,” though the U.S. needed to be “selective” about the projects it pursued.

He took a much different tone Tuesday, criticizing “speculators” in the industry for “scaring our communities” and “being aggressive with township officials, bullying our neighbors, our fellow Pennsylvanians, and refusing to listen to the people.”

“They’re threatening to fundamentally change the character of our communities,” he said, adding that the lack of legislative progress on passing new regulations for data center development — Pennsylvania’s Legislature is under split control — left him no choice but to move on the executive order.

He called out specific data center proposals he has opposed, one of them in Montgomery County, where he lives, saying a developer was trying to “bully his way into forcing data center projects through local opposition from the community and local officials.”
“I’m a hell no on that project,” he said, adding, “I’m a hell no on many other projects.”
Repeatedly, he credited his evolution on data centers to conversations he has had with concerned Pennsylvania residents, saying the “feedback I’ve gotten ... has shaped my perspective on this.”

Democrats and Republicans both are recalibrating on data center development as opposition has ramped up across the midterm landscape. Opponents have expressed concerns about the potential for rising power bills, environmental worries or fears over the growth of AI technology, among other concerns.
In New York, Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul last month signed a moratorium on data center development, while in Texas, Republican Gov. Greg Abbott paused audit data center projects this month.

In multiple contested general election fights across the map, candidates are battling over whether they support full-scale moratoriums on the developments, favor greater local control or want to extend incentives for further development.

The rapid growth of data centers, which are needed to power the AI boom, has been a core component of President Donald Trump’s economic agenda. His administration has promoted the “Ratepayer Protection Pledge,” in which developers who have signed on fund the cost of increased power generation and infrastructure for the developments. Trump has in recent weeks argued for voters to give the developments a warmer embrace, touting benefits that come with them.

The industry has pointed to potential job growth and increased tax revenue for localities that accept the developments, as well as potential property tax cuts, among other incentives. Leaders have also argued that environmental concerns have been overblown or are based on faulty data.

“Part of the challenge here is how quickly the industry has moved,” Dan Diorio, executive vice president of state policy and government affairs for the Data Center Coalition, said in a recent interview.

“And so the opposition, I think, has moved just as quickly,” he added. “Now it’s coming upon us and certainly others to bring the facts and the data to bear but also be out there and demonstrate how this industry invests in the communities for the long term.”
Following his announcement Tuesday, Shapiro was asked whether he regretted his state’s earlier approach to data center development.

“Again, there are only about five projects that have even received permits to go forward,” he said. “The problem is there’s 100 projects or so that are wreaking havoc on our communities that are never going to be built. What we’re doing today is taking concrete action to listen to the voices of the people, to put local leaders back in charge of their communities and to make very, very clear what the rules of the road are to be able to do business here in Pennsylvania.”

title: What two under-the-radar DNC moves say about the party’s direction: From the Politics Desk
summary: In today’s edition, Natasha Korecki files a dispatch from the recent Democratic National Committee meeting in Austin. Plus, we preview the key primaries to keep an eye on before polls close tonight.
story: Welcome to From the Politics Desk, a daily newsletter that brings you the NBC News Politics team’s latest reporting and analysis from the White House, Capitol Hill and the campaign trail.

In today’s edition, Natasha Korecki files a dispatch from the recent Democratic National Committee meeting in Austin, Texas. Plus, we preview the key primaries to keep an eye on before polls close tonight.
Sign up to receive this newsletter in your inbox every weekday here.
— Adam Wollner
What two under-the-radar DNC moves say about the party’s direction
AUSTIN, Texas — The big news coming out of the Democratic National Committee’s summer meeting over the weekend was that the party set its 2028 presidential primary calendar.
But some Democrats say they see significance in a pair of resolutions the DNC advanced that didn’t get as much attention.

The committee greenlit a measure supporting the abolishment of the Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency. It also passed a resolution supporting the Leahy Laws, which call for the U.S. not to fund nations that commit human rights violations.
It’s important to note the DNC doesn’t set party policy and its resolutions do not dictate the formal party platform. But these measures can serve as an indication of where the party is leaning.

For the ICE-related resolution, the DNC endorsed what not long ago was considered a fringe position. As recently as this spring, DNC members were unable to advance any measure calling for ICE to be abolished, instead settling on pushing for reforms.

DNC member Michele Johnson of Louisiana, who sponsored both the ICE and Leahy Laws resolutions, said she had changed her view on ICE as she watched incidents in Minneapolis and other cities play out between residents and immigration officers.

“Over the course of last year I began moving away from reform to abolition,” Johnson said in an interview. “This is a rogue agency, they are killing people, they are killing U.S. citizens, they have to be held accountable.”
The Leahy Law resolution didn’t have the word “Israel” in it — another issue that has divided the party — and Johnson said the intent was to address the issue in a broader sense.

“I left it without mentioning any country specifically because we shouldn’t be funding any countries that are committing human rights violations,” Johnson said. “There’s many countries that this applies to.”
“We need to make sure that when we are spending money, we are spending it on things that are morally right and morally just,” she continued.

But Sam Rosenthal, the political director at the grassroots advocacy group Roots Action, said he saw the Leahy Laws resolution passage as a step toward re-evaluating the relationship between the U.S. and Israel.

“It is an attempt to go back to basics. Can the DNC commit to holding up U.S. law? Given that, what does that mean?” Rosenthal said. He added that he hopes this is the first in a “series of steps to rebuild consensus around the DNC’s stance on what the Israel-U.S. relationship should look like.”

Rosenthal said he was heartened by the debate over abolishing ICE, saying it gave “the most hope for a progressive turn in the party.” While the DNC in a separate resolution also called only for reforms to the agency, Rosenthal chalked that up to some Democrats wanting political cover ahead of the midterms.

“The fact that DNC members wanted to go on the record with the vote is the recognition that the base is shifting. They want to meet the base where they are,” he said. “It’s the sort of resolution that I don’t think we would have made it through the DNC just — even a few months ago.”
While DNC Chair Ken Martin emphasized resolutions are not binding, he noted that Democrats had a lot to say about immigration enforcement under the Trump administration.

“Our official party positions are determined at the convention every four years in our platform. However, clearly, the one thing that unites Democrats, regardless of their position on reform versus abolish or whatever other ways to change what’s happening, is people believe that what ICE is doing right now — and CBP and the federal government — should stop,” Martin said in a statement. “There has to be a better way.”
What to watch in tonight’s primaries
If it’s Tuesday, it’s another multistate primary day.
Voters are heading to the polls in Alaska, Florida and Wyoming, while California’s 14th District will pick a replacement for former Democratic Rep. Eric Swalwell, who resigned earlier this year.
Here are a few key races to keep an eye on.

Alaska Senate: A crowded field of candidates is competing to take on GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan in November. Alaska has an all-party primary system, with the top four vote-getters advancing to a general election decided by ranked-choice voting.

The primary ballot features 16 candidates, including seven Republicans and four Democrats, with Democratic leaders touting former Rep. Mary Peltola as a strong recruit. Peltola lost re-election in 2024 by 3 points as President Donald Trump carried Alaska by 13 points.

Sullivan has been endorsed by Trump, but he faces a unique obstacle — a Republican candidate named Dan J. Sullivan is also on the primary ballot. His run sparked a legal battle over his placement on the ballot and an investigation involving state and federal prosecutors. Florida governor: The top Republican contender to succeed Gov. Ron DeSantis is Rep. Byron Donalds, who is endorsed by Trump and has attracted millions in donations from wealthy megadonors.

The field also includes Lt. Gov. Jay Collins, former House Speaker Paul Renner and James Fishback, an investment firm CEO whose openly racist comments have attracted attention in the race. DeSantis has not endorsed in the primary, but he has praised Renner.
The Democratic field is led by David Jolly, a former Republican congressman and prominent Trump critic who left the GOP in 2018.
Florida’s 19th District: The primary to replace Donalds has attracted a large group of Republican transplants.
Two previously served in Congress in other state delegations, but both left Washington under a shroud of scandal: former North Carolina Rep. Madison Cawthorn and former Rep. Chris Collins.

Trump is backing a different candidate: Catalina Lauf, a former Illinois congressional candidate who also has the support of a handful of members of Congress. Other candidates in the race include former Illinois state Sen. Jim Oberweis, who is self-funding his bid and once defeated Lauf in an Illinois congressional primary; Ola Hawatmeh, a former congressional aide who previously ran for Congress in New York; and Jim Schwartzel, a conservative talk radio station owner who has loaned his campaign $1 million and is a Florida native.

title: ‘Dune: Part Three’ sets off early ticket frenzy as fans crash sales sites
summary: Fans eager to see “Dune: Part Three” on the biggest screens in December first had to survive the online ticket queue.
story: Fans eager to see “Dune: Part Three” on the biggest screens in December first had to survive the online ticket queue.
Many on social media reported long waits and ticketing site crashes Tuesday as they scrambled to snag seats for early IMAX 70 mm screenings in December.
“Am I tripping or did every website for Dune 3 IMAX 70MM crash?” an X user wrote.

“Help! Has anybody beaten this bug/error to secure Dune 3 tickets???” another person asked, sharing a screenshot of the Fandango site with a message that read: “Internal server error. Please try again.”
“I HAVE THREE DEVICES OPEN TRYING TO GET DUNE TICKETS AND NONE OF THEM WORK,” another X user said.

The rollout is the latest sign of a growing frenzy around seeing major movies in specific premium formats, in which securing the right seat and screen has become an event of its own. A similar rush unfolded in June, when advance sales for Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” overwhelmed AMC’s website, with some moviegoers reporting hourslong waits.

“Dune: Part Three” is the latest installment in Warner Bros. Pictures’ adaptation of Frank Herbert’s seminal 1965 novel set thousands of years in the future in a world devastated by ecological collapse. The movie, directed by Denis Villeneuve, picks up 17 years after the previous one, with Paul Atreides (played by Timothée Chalamet) ruling the galaxy while in a political marriage to Princess Irulan (Florence Pugh).
The sci-fi franchise, which also stars Zendaya and Jason Momoa, has become an audience must-see since the first installment’s box-office success in 2021.
Though the new film isn’t being released until Dec. 18, some fans had already bragged about getting their tickets in April when IMAX first released a limited number of tickets for some screenings.
Last week, IMAX sent out an email telling fans to “Save the Date” for another chance to get early tickets.

“Dear IMAX fans, You showed up in a big way when the first DUNE: PART THREE tickets were released,” the email read. “We’ve heard you and know you want more access to tickets and more time to plan. So, here you go... The next opportunity to get DUNE: PART THREE tickets will arrive in one week on Tuesday, August 18 at 9:00 a.m. PST. This ticket drop will unlock more opening week DUNE Insider Screenings in IMAX and IMAX 70mm, so mark your calendars, make your plans, and get ready to return to Arrakis.”

By Tuesday, people’s efforts to secure tickets had turned into viral mayhem. Fans reported that at certain points, AMC’s and Fandango’s apps had crashed. (AMC and Fandango did not immediately respond to requests for comment Tuesday.)

Several people who managed to get tickets said it took them over an hour of waiting. A person on X posted a picture of a line wrapped around an AMC in New York, where fans tried to secure tickets in person. Some people also began reselling their early tickets on eBay for up to $1,000.

The demand for multiformat viewing experiences is fueling moviegoing FOMO, reshaping how studios market tentpole films and prompting an effort to bring order to an increasingly crowded premium-screen landscape.
Some frustrated cinephiles argue theater chains and studios should do more to ensure a smoother ticketing process.

“If you’re going to turn movie ticket-buying into a competitive sport, then you need to have the tech and UX to support that shift,” film critic Barry Hertz wrote on X. “Theatrical exhibition is not easy, certainly, but it doesn’t need to be this hard.”

AMC CEO Adam Aron addressed fan frustration Tuesday on X. He said that “ticketing traffic across AMC’s website and mobile app reached levels approximately three times higher than what we experienced during the Spider-Man: Brand New Day ticket launch, which itself followed strong advance sales for The Odyssey ticket launch before that.”
“It’s not that our systems totally failed,” he added. “We have been selling enormous numbers of tickets today, but when any of our customers experience less than our best, it is just not right.”
Aron wrote that while there was “much discussion internally” and preparation for the ticket launch, “We thought we were ready, but we weren’t.”
The theater chain, Aron said, requires “about $2 million of IT programming resource” to “fully address the issue.”

“Of course, that money has been approved already,” he wrote, “and we’ve asked our IT team to move at a whirlwind speed to take whatever steps are needed so that our ticketing systems are — in all situations and in all quantities —again top shelf.”

title: Tick prevention for dogs: Vets explain how to beat the blood-suckers
summary: Dogs are more vulnerable to Lyme disease than ever. These are the best vet-approved tick preventatives for dogs and how to check your dog for ticks.
story: You can’t completely prevent your dog from encountering ticks — populations are growing, causing the blood-suckers to show up in backyards and parks, not just deeply wooded areas. However, you can take steps to protect your pet and reduce the likelihood that they’ll get a potentially dangerous illness like Lyme disease, which is more common than you might think. In fact, about one out of every 30 dogs has tested positive this year, according to the Companion Animal Parasite Council. Read on to learn about the best tick preventatives for dogs according to veterinarians, and other steps you can take to stop the parasites from hitching a ride on your pet.

The best tick preventatives for dogs

There’s a handful of ways to protect your dog from ticks, but routinely checking them for the parasites and putting them on a year-round preventative are the most important. It’s also crucial to get them vaccinated against Lyme disease, which is the most common tick-borne disease and the only one that there’s a vaccine for, says Dr. Lindsay Kendrick, the medical director at VEG ER for Pets in Boston.

Before answering all your tick-related questions below, I curated a list of products that you’ll need to check for and prevent the parasites. A note about the tick preventatives on this list: I added options that meet expert guidance; are highly-rated; repel and/or kill multiple types of parasites; and are EPA- or FDA-approved. Some tick preventatives are sold over-the-counter, but many are only available via a prescription, which you’ll need to get from your vet.
Tweezerman Pet Flea Comb

The easiest way to check for ticks is running your hand over your dog’s body and feeling for bumps, but to be even more precise, use a fine-toothed comb. As you drag it through your pet’s coat, it surfaces ticks, which tend to be quite small, so you can easily see them. Young ticks in particular are tiny, so you may not feel them on your dog’s body but find them with a comb, says Kendrick. She added that the comb is a must for dogs with thick coats — all that padding makes ticks easy to miss.

Tweezerman’s comb is technically made for finding fleas, but it works for ticks, too. It has stainless steel bristles with rounded tips that are gentle on skin, and a handle that’s big enough to get your hand around for a comfortable grip.
TiCK MiTT

My dog has a very thin, short coat, so I can’t use a comb when I check her for ticks. Instead, I rely on the Tick Mitt, which is a glove made from a special type of textured fabric — the brand says it works like Velcro for parasites sitting on people and pets’ skin, as well as those clinging onto clothes, shoes and other items. You put the mitt on your hand and slowly sweep it across your dog’s body, inspecting it between passes to remove any ticks you caught.

The Tick Mitt works best for dogs with short coats, according to the brand, but if your dog has a thick and/or long coat, brush them first, then use the mitt to grab any ticks that surfaced. It can’t remove ticks embedded into the skin’s surface — for that, use tweezers.
TickCheck Premium Dog Tick Removal Kit

You can use any tweezers to remove ticks from your dog’s skin, but you might want to keep a dedicated tool in your bag while you’re on the go, or put one by your door so you can get rid of parasites before entering your home. TickCheck’s Tick Removal Kit comes with two stainless steel tools in a little case: a fine-tip tweezer for removing small ticks and a grabber tool for removing larger ticks that are deeply embedded in the skin. The set also comes with a card that helps you identify what type of tick you likely found.
NexGard Chewables Flea and Tick Protection

All the dog parents at NBC Selected, myself included, give our pets NexGard’s Chewable Flea and Tick Protection every month and have been doing so for years. They’re FDA-approved to kill multiple types of ticks, as well as fleas. The chewables are beef-flavored, so my dog thinks they’re standard treats and eats them immediately.
NexGard requires a prescription from your veterinarian, which the online retailer you purchase from will collect at checkout.
Frontline Plus Flea and Tick Topical Treatment

Frontline Plus’ Flea and Tick Topical Treatment, which comes in pre-measured applicators, are FDA-approved to kill ticks as well as fleas and chewing lice. To use it, you part the hair at your dog’s shoulder blades and squeeze out what’s inside one applicator. You have to keep your dog dry for 24 hours post-application — after that, the topical treatment is waterproof for a month, according to the brand. It comes in packs of three, six and eight.
Seresto Flea and Tick Collar for Dogs

Think of over-the-counter tick collars as an additional layer of protection against the parasites, not your dog’s primary preventative, says Kendrick. She recommends giving your dog a prescription preventative year-round, like the chewable and topical ones I recommend above, and putting a tick collar, like Seresto’s, on them if you’re bringing them into wooded or grassy areas. That’s exactly what I do — knowing that my dog has two lines of defense against ticks when we’re outside gives me peace of mind, especially during the peak season.

Seresto’s tick collar, which also protects dogs against fleas, is adjustable and unclasps as needed. It comes in two sizes: one for dogs under 18 pounds and one for dogs over 18 pounds. I only use the collar when I take my dog to grassy, woodsy outdoor areas, so when I’m not using it, I keep it in the sealed container it comes in because it lasts for up to eight months, according to the brand.
Checking your dog for ticks: when, how and what requires a vet visit

During tick season, which is usually from April to September, check your dog for the parasites daily, says Dr. Susanne Heartsill, the U.S. director of companion animal veterinary services at Ceva Animal Health. Be extra thorough after outdoor activities like walks, trips to the park and hikes, especially if you’re visiting grassy, wooded areas.

While ticks are more prevalent during the warmer months, they can stay active for longer, and in some parts of the country, they’re a year-round concern. Overall, the more you check your dog, the better. Heartsill also recommends using resources like the Companion Animal Parasite Council’s Parasite Prevalence Maps to monitor the prevalence of tick-borne diseases among dogs in your area to evaluate their risk level.

Checking your dog for ticks is simple: Slowly run your hand over their body and feel for bumps. If you feel one, part the fur and look closely at it. Ticks are typically the size of a pencil eraser (although they can be smaller or bigger), and they look similar to black, brown, gray or red spiders, says Kendrick. You can also use a fine-toothed comb (like the one I recommend above) to check your pet for ticks, which is especially helpful if they have a thick coat — the comb surfaces ticks that might be deeply buried in hair or fur, making them more visible, says Kendrick.

Ticks are often easier to spot after they feed on your dog’s blood because they get bigger, says Heartsill. She also recommends looking for unusual skin bumps, red or irritated areas, scabs and bites — that’s all evidence that the parasite may have been feeding on them.
Check every part of your dog’s body for ticks, but the parasites like warm, moist areas, so pay extra attention to the following spots:
Around the earsUnder and around the collar and/or harnessBetween the toesAround and under the tailAround the neckThe armpit areaThe groin areaAround the eyes and lips
Around the ears
Under and around the collar and/or harness
Between the toes
Around and under the tail
Around the neck
The armpit area

If you see a tick on your dog, remove it immediately. Pluck it off their skin with tweezers or a specialized tick removal tool like those I recommend above: Use the pointed end to grip the tick as close to the skin as possible and pull directly up with steady, even pressure, says Heartsill. Your goal is to remove the tick in one piece, so don’t twist, crush or squeeze its body. Find more tick removal tips here from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

Once the tick is off your dog, put it in a tightly-sealed plastic bag and bring it to your vet. They can run tests on the tick to see what types of diseases it carries, if any, says Kedrick. If you can’t bring it to your vet, flush it down the toilet.

Also, be sure to carefully check yourself, other people and other pets in your home if your dog has a tick. Unlike fleas, ticks don’t typically infest indoor spaces, so you won’t have to treat your home, but check everyone living there to make sure they’re not carrying a tick inside.

No, at-home tick removal remedies don’t work, and many of them can actually increase the chance of irritation and disease transmission, says Heartsill. For example, don’t burn the tick with a match or lighter, or cover it in substances like petroleum jelly, nail polish or alcohol in an attempt to make it detach on its own — it’s not helpful whatsoever.

Finding a tick on your dog isn’t a “rush to the vet” situation, says Kendrick. If you’re having trouble removing the tick, if the affected area looks infected or if your dog is showing signs of illness, make an appointment right away. But if not, let your vet know that you removed a tick from your dog and whether you see any skin irritation. Veterinarians screen for Lyme disease and other tick-borne diseases during dogs’ annual bloodwork, but yours might recommend doing a panel sooner if your dog had a tick on them. Tick-borne diseases can take months to show up on bloodwork, so tell your vet when you removed the parasite to schedule testing accordingly.
How to choose a tick preventative for dogs

No preventative completely eliminates your dog’s risk for tick-borne diseases, but using one regularly significantly reduces the likelihood of transmission, says Heartsill. Below, I broke down what experts recommend thinking about while choosing a tick preventative for your dog — be sure to consult your vet, too. Two important reminders: Always administer whatever tick preventative you buy according to the label’s directions, and check the expiration date beforehand to make sure the ingredients are still active and effective.

Buy a preventative that’s specifically made for dogs. Never give your dog something that’s formulated for cats, says Heartsill. If a product is safe for both species, it will explicitly say so.Choose the type of preventative that’s easiest to administer and works for your household. There’s three types of tick preventatives for dogs: oral medications, topical medications and tick collars. (I broke down what each one is and how they work here.) Oral and topical medications are the most effective options, while tick collars act as a secondary layer of protection in environments that are highly populated with ticks. When deciding whether an oral or topical tick preventative is right for your pet, think about what you’ll find easiest to give them and whether you have other pets in your home. Oral medications are suitable for single- and multi-pet homes, but topical medications work best for single-pet homes where the liquid solution can’t accidentally get on or be ingested by other dogs and cats.Match a preventative to your dog’s age and weight. Each one indicates what ages it’s safe for and is labeled with a weight range. Be extra cautious with old and young pets, as well as those that are pregnant and/or nursing.Look for EPA- and FDA- approval statements. Some tick products are regulated by the Environmental Protection Agency, while others are regulated by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Medications and pesticides must meet U.S. government-required safety standards before they’re sold, so look for an EPA or FDA approval statement and number somewhere on products’ packaging.Prioritize preventatives that repel and kill ticks. That means they discourage ticks from attaching to your dog in the first place, while also killing any that bite and start feeding on your pet, says Heartsill. Some preventatives just kill ticks, which is still effective at preventing disease. But preventing attachment helps reduce how many ticks crawl onto their body and can possibly get carried into your home.

Oral and topical medications are the most effective options, while tick collars act as a secondary layer of protection in environments that are highly populated with ticks. When deciding whether an oral or topical tick preventative is right for your pet, think about what you’ll find easiest to give them and whether you have other pets in your home. Oral medications are suitable for single- and multi-pet homes, but topical medications work best for single-pet homes where the liquid solution can’t accidentally get on or be ingested by other dogs and cats.

Match a preventative to your dog’s age and weight. Each one indicates what ages it’s safe for and is labeled with a weight range. Be extra cautious with old and young pets, as well as those that are pregnant and/or nursing.

Look for EPA- and FDA- approval statements. Some tick products are regulated by the Environmental Protection Agency, while others are regulated by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Medications and pesticides must meet U.S. government-required safety standards before they’re sold, so look for an EPA or FDA approval statement and number somewhere on products’ packaging.

Prioritize preventatives that repel and kill ticks. That means they discourage ticks from attaching to your dog in the first place, while also killing any that bite and start feeding on your pet, says Heartsill. Some preventatives just kill ticks, which is still effective at preventing disease. But preventing attachment helps reduce how many ticks crawl onto their body and can possibly get carried into your home.

Oral medications are made with insecticides that get transmitted to and kill ticks when they bite your dog’s skin. Chewable and swallowable tick preventatives for dogs are available over-the-counter and via a prescription. Kendrick recommends only buying those you get via a prescription because they’re safer and more effective. Topical medications, most of which are available over-the-counter, come as pre-dosed liquid solutions that you apply to your dog’s skin. Some options spread throughout the hair and skin, so ticks die when they land on your dog’s coat. Other options get absorbed by the skin and circulate through the bloodstream, killing ticks when they bite your dog. Tick collars, which are available over-the-counter, emit active ingredients that repel and kill the parasites. The collar sits on your dog’s neck, and overtime, their skin and hair absorb the ingredients and distribute them across the body. These collars work through contact, so ticks don’t have to bite your pet to die — as long as your pet is wearing it, landing on their hair or skin kills the parasites.

Frequently asked questions

Ticks are small parasites that feed on humans’ and animals’ (a.k.a. their hosts) blood, says Heartsill. They’re part of the arachnid family, so they’re more closely related to spiders than insects. When ticks bite humans and animals to feed on their blood, it can irritate skin, as well as potentially spread diseases like Lyme disease, making hosts sick.

For the most part, dogs (and people) encounter ticks outdoors. The parasites mainly live in tall grass, wooded areas, brush and leaf litter, but you can find them almost anywhere now that their populations are expanding, including backyards, hiking trails and parks. Ticks don’t jump or fly: They wait on vegetation and attach to people and animals that brush by.

Ticks can be harmful to dogs, but they aren’t always because not all of them carry disease. If your dog is bit by a tick that doesn’t carry disease, they might have minor skin irritation afterward, but that’s it. If a disease-carrying tick attaches to your dog’s skin, bites them and feeds on their blood for a certain period of time, the parasite can transmit Lyme disease, ehrlichiosis, anaplasmosis, babesiosis, Rocky Mountain spotted fever and other illnesses, depending on the tick species.

Ticks have to latch onto a dog’s skin for a certain period of time to transmit disease if they’re carrying one, says Kendrick. The exact timeframe varies by disease type — for example, Lyme disease transmission usually takes more than 24 hours, according to the CDC, while anaplasmosis transmission usually takes 12 to 24 hours, according to Harvard Medical School. This emphasizes why constantly checking your dog for ticks and giving them preventatives is so important: If you find a tick on your pet, you might be able to remove it before it transmits disease, and if you give them a preventative, it will likely kill the tick before it transmits disease.

After your dog is bitten by a disease-carrying tick, it can take anywhere from days to months for them to test positive for an illness in bloodwork and show symptoms (although many dogs never show symptoms). The exact timeframe depends on the type of disease the tick was carrying, so if you find the parasite on your pet, consult your vet about next steps. Also make sure to stay up to date with your dog’s routine bloodwork, which is when vets often catch tick-borne diseases despite pet owners never finding a parasite on their pet.

Bloodwork is the only way to confirm diagnosis of a tick-borne disease, says Kendrick. That’s why vets check for illnesses like Lyme disease during dogs’ annual bloodwork — sometimes pet owners don’t see a tick on their dog or notice symptoms, but their pet tests positive for a tick-borne disease, which allows them to get the proper treatment. If you recently found a tick on your dog, your vet may suggest scheduling additional testing to be proactive.

There are a handful of symptoms associated with tick-borne diseases. The experts I talked to recommend looking out for the below — call your vet if you notice any of them, especially if you recently found a tick on your pet.
LethargyLow or complete loss of appetiteFeverJoint paint or lamenessSwollen lymph nodesLimpingWeight lossVomitingAbnormal bleeding or bruising

Fever

No, tick-borne diseases like Lyme disease cannot spread between dogs or other pets in your home, including cats, says Kendrick. Your pets can only get a tick-borne disease if they’re bitten by a tick carrying a certain disease.
No, people cannot get tick-borne diseases from dogs. You can only get a tick-borne disease if you’re bitten by a tick carrying a certain disease.

No, you shouldn’t put bug spray of any kind on your dog, who could react poorly to the ingredients in the formula, says Kenrick. Stick to preventatives meant for dogs, and prioritize FDA/EPA-approved options.

Yes, cats can get ticks and tick-borne diseases, but those who go outside are the most at risk, says Kendrick. If your cat goes outside, follow the same tick precautions you do with your dog, including giving them a feline-specific preventative year-round and checking their skin whenever they come inside.

If you have indoor cats, it’s highly unlikely that they’ll encounter ticks, so they’re at a low risk of getting a tick-borne disease. Make sure you thoroughly check yourself and your dog, as well as other items like bags and shoes, before you come inside to make sure you’re not carrying ticks into your home — that’s generally the only way indoor cats encounter them.

Yes, tick season is getting worse. Concerns around ticks have recently increased due to their growing populations, especially in places that aren’t typically considered tick hot spots. These parasites thrive in warm, humid environments, which more parts of the country now experience for longer periods of time. Some areas are also having milder winters than usual, which extends the timeframe during which ticks typically survive and remain active for.

Additionally, people and their pets are encountering ticks more often as neighborhoods expand into habitats where wildlife like deer, rodents, rabbits and coyotes live, says Heartsill. These animals serve as hosts for ticks, so if you’re sharing backyards, walking paths, parks and other green spaces with them, ticks are certainly present. It’s not just wooded areas you have to worry about anymore.

I’m also a pet parent who has a dog and two cats. To write this article, I interviewed two veterinarians about health risks dogs face when exposed to ticks, how to protect them from ticks and preventatives to avoid illness.

title: Suspect in Chucky-style mask wanted in Philadelphia after chasing jogger, police say
summary: A 40-year-old female jogger was chased by what appeared to be a fan of the slasher franchise, police said.
story: Philadelphia police asked for the public’s help Tuesday to find a person who they said donned a Chucky-style horror mask and “made threatening comments” while chasing a woman near City Hall last week.

The strange incident unfolded around 5:30 a.m. Wednesday, when a 40-year-old female jogger in athletic wear “was chased by a masked offender” near 1500 John F. Kennedy Blvd., Philadelphia police said in a statement.
The masked person held a phone in front of the woman and repeatedly asked, “Are you ready to die?” police told NBC Philadelphia.
“The offender made threatening comments as they approached causing the complainant to stumble and sustain injury,” the police statement said.

Minutes earlier, the masked person had been spotted harassing pedestrians near 15th and Chestnut streets and being denied service at a Dunkin’ location, Philadelphia Police Capt. Jason Smith told NBC Philadelphia.
The masked person, carrying a distinctive blue plaid backpack, was last seen ducking into SEPTA’s Suburban Station.

Police believe the masked person is a man who is about 5-feet-8 and 16 to 20 years old, “wearing a white baby doll style Halloween mask with black hair, and a black/blue plaid backpack,” according to the statement.
Investigators released video and images of the masked person.
The person was wearing a “Chucky doll Halloween-style face mask,” Smith said, referring to the killer doll from the “Child’s Play” horror movie franchise.
There had been no arrests as of early Tuesday afternoon.
Police warned in the statement that if “you see this suspect do not approach, contact 911 immediately.”

While no one was seriously injured in the incident, it had some similarities to a scary situation near St. Louis two weeks ago, in which a 15-year-old boy was accused of stabbing a 78-year-old man to death while dressed as a creepy clown.
The suspect was charged with murder in the killing of John Wesley Allen, whose body was found near a bus stop in East St. Louis, Illinois.
Allen, who lived in a retirement community in St. Louis, regularly took the bus to visit his sister in East St. Louis, family members said.
Shortly before the slaying, neighborhood doorbell video obtained by NBC affiliate KSDK showed a person dressed as a clown looking into the camera and saying, “I have a gift for you.”
Neighbors told the station that they saw the person going door to door with a large knife.

title: Teacher says 8-foot python blamed by officials for Virginia school fire is innocent
summary: “The snake contributed to starting the fire,” the fire marshal said. “However, I don’t think there was any maliciousness involved on the snake’s side.”
story: Firefighters battling a blaze at a Bedford County, Virginia, middle school encountered more than just smoke. Hiding underneath a desk in a classroom was an 8-foot python, which fire officials say started the inferno.
But a life science teacher who took ownership of the snake, named Nanner, has hit back at the claims, saying the fire was an accident, not her or anyone else’s fault.

“I am devastated for many reasons right now — all of my teaching tools are now gone, many children will now not have the opportunities that many others have had, 18 years of teaching material is gone,” Brittany Jacobs said on Facebook. “I never wanted this for my school, my admin, or my county.”
She insists Nanner broke out of her tank after the fire had already started and fled the classroom to escape the heat.
“She pushed on the screen so hard to get out that she bent the metal locks. ... She left the room because it was so hot in there. So hot that it melted the tank next to hers,” Jacobs wrote.
